name: Goal map
summary: See every goal and what feeds it on one canvas, with the path the risk runs along.

rebuild.builds: The Goal map, as a feature a workspace can switch off: one of Goals' layouts, drawing every goal on a canvas, north stars at the top, solid lines for feeds into and dotted for also helps, with the critical path bold and each goal's roll-up of what feeds it. It owns no records. Off, Goals offers List, Table, Board and History, and a link or saved view that asked for the Map (view=map) opens the List and says once “The Goal map is off here, so this is the List.”
entry: Goals' layouts and the roll-up of what feeds a goal are the core's (stage 3); the map draws them and adds nothing to them.
exit: Switched off, Goals' Layout offers List, Table, Board and History, and nothing on Goals says Map (journey U165).
Switched off, /goals?view=map opens the List with “The Goal map is off here, so this is the List.” once; switched back on, the same address opens the Map (journey U165, check N22).
gaps: The Goal map is a switch, not yet a folder of its own (SW5 moves it): its screen (src/screens/GoalMap.tsx), the drawing half of src/domain/map.ts and the Map layout's control in src/screens/GoalsScreen.tsx are still the core's. src/app/reads.ts goalMapOn is the one place that asks whether it is on; the rule that opens the List instead is src/domain/query.ts layoutOn.
It has no page of its own yet (/goals/map is SW5's), so its switched-off line is the List's sentence, not a not-found page.
